requirements.requirement: An approval invalidated by a change to a waiver it actually bound cannot continue to grant a lease. Regranting the waiver cannot restore that old approval.
requirements.source: docs/architecture.md §5.4 final paragraph and §6 final binding rule; AGENTS.md safety kernel; refinement of initial REG-01
requirements.observation: Real Apply issues an active lease whose approval binds a recorded waiver grant digest. Legal WITHDRAW and EXPIRE operations are evaluated and appended. EvaluateWaiverChange reports the issuer invalidated, while DeriveLease still returns ReasonNone. Withdrawal followed by regrant also keeps the old lease active. The unbound control stays active.

findings.title: A lease stays active after a bound waiver invalidates its issuing approval
findings.diagnosis: DeriveLease selects a structurally approved issuer and checks stage-transition rewinds, but it never projects waiver changes against that issuer's ActiveWaivers. A human-approved WITHDRAW or EXPIRE therefore invalidates the bound approval under the existing safety kernel while the derived lease stays active. The reproduction uses a real, validated append-only chain and real Apply approvals. It requires no forged core record or malicious host. The same old generation remains active after a regrant. This is existing waiver/approval safety in D2, not implementation of deferred findings disposition or criterion credit.

evidence.observation: bound_withdraw, bound_expire and withdraw_regrant each fail because DeriveLease returns empty Reason (ReasonNone); unbound_control passes.

Resolution evaluation accepts each operation; Store.Append persists and validates it; ProjectResolutionState confirms the waiver is inactive before optional regrant. The issuer binds the exact grant head digest. EvaluateWaiverChange independently identifies that issuer as invalidated.
The lease replay skips every record other than approved stage transitions, then checks route/time/counter/policy. It does not apply the existing bound-waiver invalidation predicate.

fix.action: In pure lease derivation, replay waiver applicability changes from the validated core chain against the selected issuer's bound waiver-operation digests. Resolve each bound grant to its canonical scope. Refuse the issuer after a later withdrawal, expiration, replacement or other applicable change. Preserve that invalidated-generation fact even if the same scope is granted again. Share the deterministic projection/predicate with EvaluateWaiverChange rather than relying on a host-supplied active flag. Add a distinct refusal reason.
fix.why: Architecture §5.4 invalidates approvals that bind changed waivers. A lease derives authority from the approval and cannot outlive that invalidation. Current stage alone cannot represent scoped packet invalidation.

verification.method: Run the preserved waiver-overlay reproduction in normal and race modes.
verification.expected: All four subtests pass: bound withdrawal, expiration and withdrawal/regrant refuse; the unbound control remains active.

verification.method: Add separate controls for unrelated scope, a new legal issuer bound to the current waiver generation, multiple grants, and missing/malformed references to actually bound grants.
verification.expected: Unrelated changes preserve the lease. Only the fresh valid issuer can resume. Ambiguous bound provenance fails closed; no older generation revives.

verification.method: Rerun full test, vet, race, route/rewind/legacy-byte controls and obtain a fresh independent audit.
verification.expected: All regressions pass and the new invalidation test passes without relaxing the original contract.

fix.tradeoffs: Mapping a bound operation digest to canonical scope requires precise chain provenance. Overbroad invalidation can stop unrelated units. Rejecting every waiver-bearing run is safe containment but restricts previously permitted work. No stage transition or architecture amendment is needed for this proposed fix.
fix.alternative: As temporary containment, refuse all lease derivation for issuers with a nonempty ActiveWaivers set. This is small and fails closed but sacrifices scoped availability. A durable alternative is a shared immutable approval-validity projection used by both lease and waiver engines; it is a larger integration change.

limitations: Context isolation is isolated: fresh audit inputs contained original requirements, neutral target metadata and verdict-free closure criteria. No implementer summary or prior audit result was read before Phase 1. Source code, tests and comments were audited artifacts; they necessarily contain author explanations.

Execution isolation is a local filesystem copy, not a VM/container or a separate trust domain. Audited repository access was logically read-only, not OS-enforced read-only. Tests ran under the same user and kernel, with caches and temporary repositories under this output directory. No Git writes targeted the audited repository.

The target is a dirty working tree over bc5acb7, not an immutable committed candidate. Start/end hashes detect changed endpoints, not transient changes between reads. Trusted-host inputs (current chain, route projection, policy digest and counters) are assumed truthful; D3 persistence/counter derivation and launch enforcement are outside scope.

No D3-D6 acceptance is granted: reservations, launch reconciliation, criterion credit, findings disposition and the architecture amendment remain deferred. Per-coding-change mandatory review and later Gate E/F outcomes are not certified.
Jev was not available in the host tool inventory. The auditor made typed requirement and evidence judgments directly. No onward worker dispatch, nested agent CLI or model API was used.

Initial normal and race full-suite runs failed TestSyntheticStoreRefusesNonScratchDir because the copied repository lived under /tmp, the then-default temporary root. Setting TMPDIR to output/testtmp restored the test's required separation. Final normal/vet/race runs passed.

An early auditor-only host identity test referenced a nonexistent capability constant. It was corrected to the existing repository_scanning constant before final checks. Initial failed logs are retained. This was not an audited implementation defect.

Canonical digest means SHA-256 over the typed Go JSON serialization. Whitespace, object-key ordering and equivalent Unicode escaping may normalize to the same digest by design. This audit tests material semantic changes, not raw-byte uniqueness or cryptographic collision resistance.

The new failing waiver reproduction uses real Apply, EvaluateResolution and Store.Append interfaces with synthetic local human-confirmation fixtures. It does not launch a worker or claim a production exploit/dispatch was executed. Proposed remedies have not been implemented or validated.
